children.text: śleṣe kecana śabdagumphaviṣaye kecid rase cāpare
children.translated_text: Some [poets excel] in <s>śleṣa</s> (double entendre), some in the weaving of words,
others in <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), some in <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figuration), others in conveying meaning, and others in narrative description.
Ah! Roaming with the skill of the <s>Vindhya</s> forests of profound and majestic poetry,
shattering the frontal globes of rival poet-elephants — <s>Bāṇa</s> is a five-faced lion (<s>pañcānana</s>)! (1)

children.text: hemno bhāraśatāni vā madamucāṃ vṛndāni vā dantināṃ
children.translated_text: Hundreds of weights of gold, or herds of rutting elephants —

children.text: śrīharṣeṇa samarpitāni kavaye bāṇāya kutrādya tat /
children.translated_text: these were bestowed by King <s>Śrīharṣa</s> upon the poet <s>Bāṇa</s>; but where is all that now?

children.text: yā bāṇena tu tasya sūktinikarairuṭṭaṅkitāḥ kīrtayas
children.translated_text: Yet the fame that <s>Bāṇa</s> engraved with his collections of fine sayings —

children.text: tāḥ kalpapralaye 'pi yānti na manāṅ manye parimlānatām // 2 //
children.translated_text: that, I believe, does not fade in the slightest even at the dissolution of the world-age. (2)
Alas! I worship <s>Abhinanda</s> as the lord of meaning; I praise <s>Vākpatirāja</s> as the lord of speech;

children.text: raseśvaraṃ naumi ca kālidāsaṃ bāṇaṃ tu sarvaśvaramānato 'smi // 3 //
children.translated_text: I bow to <s>Kālidāsa</s> as the lord of <s>rasa</s>; but to <s>Bāṇa</s>, the lord of all, I offer my reverence. (3)
The goddess of speech (<s>Vāgdevī</s>) has indeed been cultivated with relish by many chief poets here;

children.text: bāṇena tu vaijātyāt kathayati nāmaiva vāṇīti // 4 //
children.translated_text: but by <s>Bāṇa</s>, on account of [her] different nature, she speaks her very name as '<s>Vāṇī</s>' [i.e., both 'Speech' and 'belonging to Bāṇa']. (4)
<s>Kādambarī</s>, [his] sister-creation, is truly nectar in the hearts of the wise;
through the <s>Harṣākhyāyikā</s> (Narrative of <s>Harṣa</s>), <s>Bāṇa</s> obtained fame like the ocean. (5)
By <s>Bāṇa</s> as his perpetual companion, who bears the form of a bow (<s>dhanus</s>),
rich in virtues (<s>guṇa</s>) [/bowstring], all people are delighted. (6)
Just as <s>Śikhaṇḍinī</s> formerly became <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> [changing from female to male], so I understand:
<s>Vāṇī</s> (the goddess of Speech) became <s>Bāṇa</s> in order to attain greater boldness. (7)
Because of <s>Bāṇa</s> [/arrow] lodged in the heart, even a slow pace
becomes the restlessness of poet-deer — the arrow (<s>bāṇa</s>) is the cause of that. (8)
<s>Subandhu</s>, <s>Bāṇabhaṭṭa</s>, and <s>Kavirāja</s> — these three
are skilled in the path of oblique expression (<s>vakrokti</s>); whether a fourth exists or not [is doubtful]. (9)
Charming with variegated, colorful brilliance of diction, the king
[<s>Śrīharṣa</s>] brought together <s>Bāṇa</s> and <s>Mayūra</s> [the arrow and the peacock], as it were. (10)
An arrow (<s>bāṇa</s>) for piercing rival poets, a peacock (<s>mayūra</s>) roaming in the dense forest of poetry,
a dear friend (<s>subandhu</s>) of the audience of connoisseurs — victorious is the illustrious <s>Bhaṭṭabāṇa</s>, the king of poets (<s>kavirāja</s>)! (11)
It is fitting that poets, having heard <s>Kādambarī</s>, have resorted to silence,
because when the sound of <s>Bāṇa</s> [/the twang of an arrow] resounds, no recitation is possible — so says the scripture. (12)
With charming sounds, letters, and words, full of <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s>, captivating the mind of the world —

children.text: tatkiṃ taruṇī nahi nahi, vāṇī bāṇasya madhuraśīlasya // 13 //
children.translated_text: is that a young woman? No, no! It is the speech of sweet-natured <s>Bāṇa</s>. (13)
Having composed the <s>Harṣacarita</s> perpetually, having crafted the tale of <s>Kādambarī</s>,
the speech of <s>Bāṇa</s> wanders freely upon the earth like a dancer. (14)
What poet can follow <s>Bāṇa</s>, the divine one (<s>gīrvāṇa</s>) among true poets?
Does a fly follow the ocean? What gem compares to the sun-jewel? (15)
Equal interweaving of word and meaning is considered the <s>Pāñcālī</s> style (<s>rīti</s>);
if that [truly exists], it is in the speech of <s>Śilābhaṭṭārikā</s> and in the utterances of <s>Bāṇa</s>. (16)

children.text: kevalo 'pi sphuran bāṇaḥ karoti vimadān kavīn /
children.translated_text: <s>Bāṇa</s> [/arrow], shining even alone, humbles poets;
how much more so when fitted with a notch and attended by the <s>Pulinda</s> [tribal archer/poetic forces]! (17)
When <s>Daṇḍin</s> [/the staff-bearer] approaches, the minds of poets at once tremble;

children.text: praviṣṭhe tvantaraṃ bāṇe kaṇṭhe vāgeva rudhyate // 18 //
children.translated_text: but when <s>Bāṇa</s> [/the arrow] enters the scene, speech itself is choked in the throat. (18)
